source.title: On some open questions in bilinear quantum control

accepted.question_text: Consider a bilinear quantum control system on a separable Hilbert space H of the form dψ/dt = (A + u(t)B)ψ, where (A,B) satisfies Assumption 1 from the paper: A is skew-adjoint with an eigenbasis (φ_k)_{k∈N}, A+uB is essentially skew-adjoint for admissible controls, and the control acts through the operator B. Assume moreover that (A,B) is k-weakly-coupled for every k > 0, so that the attainable set from any eigenvector is contained in the intersection of the domains D(|A|^k) over all k > 0. Give an explicit state ψ_b that is not colinear with the first eigenvector φ_1 and for which there exist a control u in L^1(R,R) and a time T > 0 such that the corresponding propagator satisfies Υ^u_{T,0} φ_1 = ψ_b.
accepted.context_brief: Explicit reachable state for infinitely weakly-coupled systems

evidence.quote: Most of the bilinear quantum systems we encountered in the physics literature are k-weakly-coupled for every k > 0. We have already seen that if (A, B) is k-weakly-coupled for every k > 0, then the attainable set from any eigenvector of A is contained in ∩k>0D(|A|^k), the intersection of the domains of all the iterations of A.
Question 1: Let (A, B) be k-weakly-coupled for every k > 0. Give (explicitly) a state ψb not colinear to φ1 such that there exist a control u in L1(R, R) and a time T > 0 for which ΥuT,0φ1 = ψb.

accepted.question_text: Let (A,B) satisfy Assumption 1 for the bilinear quantum system dψ/dt = (A + u(t)B)ψ, and suppose (A,B) admits a non-degenerate chain of connectedness, so the reachable set from φ_1 is dense in H. Define ρ to be the infimum of all T ≥ 0 such that the union of states reachable from φ_1 by piecewise-constant controls over times 0 ≤ t ≤ T is dense in H. Does there exist a system (A,B) that is k-weakly-coupled for every k > 0, whose drift operator A is unbounded, whose control operator B has no eigenvector, and for which the minimal approximate-controllability time satisfies ρ > 0?
accepted.context_brief: Positive minimal time in infinite-dimensional approximate control

evidence.quote: Let (A, B) satisfy Assumption 1 and admit a non-degenerate chain of connectedness. From Proposition 5, we know that ∪t≥0{Υut,0φ1|u ∈ P C} is dense in H. We define ρ = inf {T ≥ 0 such that ∪0≤t≤T {Υut,0φ1|u ∈ P C} = H}.
Question 2: Does it exist (A, B) k-weakly-coupled for every k > 0 such that A is unbounded, B has no eigenvector and ρ > 0?

accepted.question_text: Fix a bilinear quantum system dψ/dt = (A + u(t)B)ψ with first and second eigenstates φ_1 and φ_2 of the drift operator A. Suppose one imposes an a priori upper bound on the L^1 norm of the control u. Under that control-budget constraint, what is the smallest possible transfer time needed to steer the system from the first eigenstate φ_1 to the second eigenstate φ_2?
accepted.context_brief: Time-optimal transfer under an L1 control budget

evidence.quote: For weakly-coupled systems, it can be easily proved (see [31]) that an a priori bound on the L1 norm of the control is not compatible with approximate controllability in arbitrarily small time.
Question 3: An upper bound on the L1 norm of the control being given, what is the smallest possible time needed to transfer a given system (A, B) from the first eigenstate of A to the second one?

accepted.question_text: Let (A,B) satisfy Assumption 1 and admit a non-degenerate chain of connectedness. Then for every target state ψ_b on the unit sphere of H and every ε > 0, one can find a piecewise-constant control u_ε : [0,T_ε] → {0,1} such that the propagated first eigenstate Υ^{u_ε}_{T_ε,0} φ_1 is within ε of ψ_b. Existing constructions can produce such controls with a number of discontinuities of order 1/ε. Is it possible instead to construct controls u_ε whose number of discontinuities is little-o of 1/ε as ε → 0?
accepted.context_brief: Reducing the switch complexity of approximate steering controls

evidence.quote: Let (A, B) satisfy Assumption 1. If (A, B) admits a non-degenerate chain of connectedness, then for every ψb in the unit sphere of H, for every ε > 0, there exists uε : [0, Tε] → {0, 1} such that kΥuTu,0φ1 −ψbk < ε. Using [16, Proposition 3], it is possible to build uε with a number of discontinuities of the order of 1/ε.
Question 4: Is it possible to build uε with a number of discontinuities of order oε→0 (1/ε)?

accepted.question_text: Does there exist a bilinear quantum system dψ/dt = (A + u(t)B)ψ in which the control operator B is unbounded, the pair (A,B) satisfies Assumption 1, the system is not k-weakly-coupled for any k > 0, and nevertheless the infinite-dimensional dynamics can still be approximated uniformly by its Galerkin truncations with respect to the L^1 norm of the control? Here the intended uniform approximation is the same type discussed earlier in the paper for weakly-coupled systems, where for every control with bounded L^1 norm the Galerkin evolution stays uniformly close to the full evolution.
accepted.context_brief: Good Galerkin approximations beyond weak coupling

evidence.quote: Remark 1: Notice that, in Propositions 7 and 8, the upper bound of the |A|k/2 norm of the solution of (1) or the bound on the error between the infinite dimensional system and its finite dimensional approximation only depend on the L1 norm of the control, not on the time.

Question 5: Does it exist a system (A, B) with unbounded B that satisfies Assumption 1, is not k-weakly-coupled for any k > 0 and that can be approached, uniformly with respect of the L1 norm of the control, by its Galerkin approximations?
